decisions.quote: While it has been shown to support natural language code search and code documentation generation tasks, its effectiveness for code clone detection is not explored in depth. In this paper, we aim to replicate and evaluate the performance of CodeBERT for code clone detection on multiple datasets with varying functionalities to understand (1) whether CodeBERT can generalize to unseen code, (2) how fine-tuning can effect CodeBERT’s performance on unseen code, and (3) how CodeBERT performs for detecting various code clone types.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The supplied primary text contains only the title, authors, and abstract (4 lines total, without main text or bibliography). While the abstract states that the authors 'aim to replicate and evaluate the performance of CodeBERT for code clone detection on multiple datasets,' it provides no bibliographic citation or specific original empirical claim being retested, and explicitly notes that while CodeBERT was shown to support code search and documentation generation, 'its effectiveness for code clone detection is not explored in depth.' Consequently, the unresolved question is which specific published work and finding this study empirically replicates—specifically, whether target_index 0 refers to the already-shipped CodeBERT paper in input_row_index 878 (Feng et al., 2020, 'CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages,' DOI 10.18653/v1/2020.findings-emnlp.139) or a distinct prior study applying CodeBERT to code clone detection.
